summary: I recomputed every coin, card and deck change across all 21 turns, and each one follows the DESIGN and the SPEC. That covers costs, challenge swaps, first-challenger priority, eliminations, skipping eliminated seats and the last-alive win. Every seat was offered only legal options and targets, and no hidden information leaked. The gaps are in what players see and in the platform's final status: no rules brief appears in the offered prompt, the state line is full of blank and unlabeled bookkeeping, and all four seats are still shown as 'active' after the game ended.

findings.where: end of game (after round 21), all seats
findings.observed: FINAL SEAT STATUS shows 'seat 1 Ada: active, seat 2 Blaise: active, seat 3 Curie: active, seat 4 Dirac: active'. Seat 1 was eliminated in turn 8, seat 3 in turn 9 and seat 4 in turn 21, and seat 2 won.
findings.expected: Seats 1, 3 and 4 should show as eliminated or lost, and seat 2 as the winner. SPEC R29 sets alive=false and R34 names the winner, and the platform status should reflect both.
findings.fix: When the game file sets alive=false, also mark the seat eliminated to the platform, and declare seat 2 the winner at R34. If the game file already does this, then the engine is failing to map it to seat status.

findings.where: FIRST QUESTION, seat 1 (and every action question)
findings.observed: Apart from state dumps, the whole question was: 'Choose your action. Tax claims Duke, assassinate claims Assassin, steal claims Captain, exchange claims Ambassador; claims can be challenged.' Nothing says what each action gains or costs (Income 1, Foreign Aid 2, Coup 7, Tax 3, Assassinate 3, Steal 2, Exchange draw 1 / return 1). Nothing says who may block what, what a challenge costs either side, that 10+ coins forces Coup, or how the game is won, including the 40-turn cap.
findings.expected: PROMPT: the players need the rules brief from the DESIGN, covering actions, costs, blocks, challenge outcomes and the ending.
findings.fix: Include a rules brief in the system prompt or the first question. Give a one-line effect next to each option, for example 'tax: +3 coins, claims Duke'.

findings.where: every round, the private 'Your hidden cards' line to each seat
findings.observed: The line prints raw bookkeeping with empty values, such as 'action , ... block_role , ... claimed_role , ... winner .'. trace_lint counts 84 of these lines plus 4 more. It also prints 'standings [[1, 5], [2, 4], [1, 3], [2, 3]]' with no labels; these appear to be [hidden_count, coins] in seat order. The action announcement for Income/Coup reads 'Claimed role: . Target seat: 0 (0 means none).'
findings.expected: PROMPT: show only what a player can use, with labels, and never print empty fields.
findings.fix: Hide the game-level bookkeeping attributes (action, claimed_role, block_role, winner, challenger, etc.) from the private line, or skip any that are empty. Label standings or drop them, since the public per-seat blocks already carry the same data. Leave out 'Claimed role'/'Target' when they don't apply.

findings.observed: Players get their hand twice before the first decision: 'Your two hidden role cards' in round 0, then 'Your hidden cards' in round 1, with the same content. Each seat's public block repeats the header 'Seat X is the active player and the deck holds 7 cards. Coins, revealed cards and hidden card count of the other players:', which is already in the turn announcement.
findings.expected: PROMPT: avoid repeated text, and print one state summary per turn.
findings.fix: Merge the per-seat blocks into a single table under one header, and drop either the round-0 deal message or the round-1 repeat.

findings.observed: Seat 1 was asked `choose_the_card_to_reveal` with options ['Duke', 'Duke']. Seat 4 was asked `choose_the_card_to_return` with options ['Ambassador', 'Ambassador']. Both options are identical cards, so there was nothing to decide.
findings.expected: INTERFACE: ask only what needs deciding. The engine already auto-answers single-option target choices (rounds 11, 20, 21).
findings.fix: Remove duplicate card names from the options before asking, and auto-resolve when only one distinct card remains.

idea_alignment: This is still the Coup in the IDEA: hidden roles, bluffed claims (seat 4's Duke block and Duke taxes), challenges that cost the loser a card, and last player standing wins. The changes the play exercised (simultaneous single-poll reactions, first-challenger priority, draw-1/return-1 Exchange, first player starting with 1 coin) are all listed in the DESIGN with reasons.
